answer: Sybil resistance requires each agent identity to be registered to a remotely attested enclave. MRENCLAVE commits to the approved code; a hardware-rooted key and fresh attestation show it runs on genuine silicon. Copying a VM cannot copy that key or forge the hardware proof, so creating parallel identities requires acquiring additional physical silicon rather than duplicating software. The wharf policy may label onyx and canyon deployments separately, while treating MRENCLAVE as a code measurement, not a unique device identifier.
